source: BK5 printed pp.39-40 = book5-6.pdf PDF pp.45-46; Step 7 speculative derivation from topology
note: Speculative (Step 7): every expect is derived by hand from the 28 printed wires (no erratum; the errata sheet's Book V entries end at page 35) and the p.40 rule that the lights give the German sentence in the proper order. Slide-switch roles per jack-map: S/V arms, R/U close LEFT, T/W close RIGHT; target 0 = LEFT, 1000 = RIGHT. Nets: PLUS = {3S, 2S, 1S, 5A}; MINUS = {1B..6B, 1E, 2E, 3E, 4E}; P1 = {1T, 2V, 1A}; P2 = {1R, 2U, 1C, 4C}; {2W, 4A}; {2R, 3H}; {2T, 3L}; {3G, 2A}; {3J, 3C}; {3K, 2C}; {3N, 3A}; {3R, 3F, 6A}. Switch 1 picks which of P1 (Piet) or P2 (Eva + ihrem) is live; switch 2 set 2 either joins P1 and P2 (LEFT: both names, ihrem) or routes P1 to output 4 (RIGHT: seinem only with Pete); switch 2 set 1 picks the singular (RIGHT, relay 3 set 2) or plural (LEFT, relay 3 set 1) verb; switch 3 LEFT pulls relay 3 (coil 3E-3F straight across the rails) and lights output 6, which moves each verb to its past-perfect auxiliary. Relays 1, 2, 4 have nF unwired: their indicator lamps light alone across nC-nE and the relays stay out. Topology versus prose: with switch 2 RIGHT ('Pete or Eve') only the name switch 1 picks lights, so the circuit never displays both names with a singular verb and the 'oder' the page tells the reader to supply has no display; the fixture asserts the circuit, not the prose. The script walks all eight switch settings in Gray order from all-RIGHT; switches are set before power-on so the first state is not the default switch position. The 500 ms advance before each expect lets lamps and relay 3 finish their transients; the page states no timing.

script.cite: BK5 printed p.40 = book5-6.pdf PDF p.46, stated rule: the lights give the German sentence in the proper order (switch 1 RIGHT Pete / LEFT Eve; switch 2 RIGHT Pete or Eve / LEFT Pete and Eve; switch 3 RIGHT present / LEFT past perfect; output light 1 Piet, relay light 1 Eva, output 2 haben mit, relay 2 hat mit, output 3 spielt mit, relay 3 spielen mit, output 4 seinem, relay 4 ihrem, output 5 Ball, output 6 gespielt); p.39 (PDF p.45) 'incorporates the word order requirements of the past perfect tense with the selection rule for the appropriate adjective'; derived from topology: rails: 3S/3+ makes arms 3S, 2S, 1S plus (2S/3S, 1S/2S); 6B/6- with the B chain and 1B/1E, 1E/2E, 2E/3E, 3E/4E puts 1B-6B and 1E-4E on minus; 5A/5+ lights output 5 (Ball) always; coils 1, 2, 4 have nF unwired so relays 1, 2, 4 never pull and their lamps light alone across nC-nE; switches 1, 2, 3 RIGHT (Pete, or, present): 1S-1T feeds 2V (1T/2V) and output 1 (1A/2V) = Piet; 2V-2W feeds 4A (2W/4A) = seinem; 2U dead (1R open), relay lights 1 and 4 dark; 2S-2T feeds 3L (2T/3L), relay 3 out (3R open, 3F dead) so 3L-3N feeds 3A (3A/3N) = spielt mit; 2R dead so 3H, 3C, 2A dark; 3F/6A dead, output 6 off; sentence 'Piet spielt mit seinem Ball'
script.quote: Read the German sentence from the lights as indicated above. The German sentence will be in the proper order and will be complete except for the conjunction which must be supplied if Pete and Eve are indicated as input: supply "und" for "and"; "oder" for "or."
